'''''Star Wars: Galactic Defense''''' was a [[Wikipedia:Tower defense|tower defense]] mobile game developed by [[DeNA]] Santiago for [[Wikipedia:Android (operating system)|Android]] and [[Wikipedia:iOS|iOS]]. The game took place in a wide variety of eras, spanning both the [[Prequel trilogy|prequel]] and the [[Original trilogy|original]] trilogies.<ref name="Diary" />

The game was announced on [[September 24]], [[2014]], and released on [[October 30]], 2014. In mid-[[February]] [[2016]], DeNA announced the release of 10 new missions on the [[planet]] [[Coruscant]], along with the eventual shutdown of the game. On [[March 6]], 2016, the game was no longer available for download. Eventually, DeNA shut down the game's servers, rendering it unplayable.

==Publisher's summary==
''Experience the ''Star Wars'' universe as an elite tower defense force in the free mobile game ''Star Wars: Galactic Defense''. This game propels the traditional tower defense genre into a galaxy far, far away by seamlessly blending iconic characters, adrenaline-fueled battles, and strategic gameplay into an exciting one of a kind mobile experience.''

==Gameplay==
'''Planet Introductions'''
*[[Tatooine]] (10 levels): "When [[Alliance Intelligence/Legends|rebel spies]] obtain information that could lead to the destruction of the [[Galactic Empire|Empire's]] [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station|new secret weapon]], the two forces engage in battle on the surface of this arid and hot desert world."
*[[Hoth]] (10 levels): "The [[Alliance to Restore the Republic|Rebel Alliance]] has established a [[Echo Base|base]] on this desolate world covered in ice and snow, but the Empire has discovered is location and has prepared a [[Battle of Hoth|large-scale ground assault]] to destroy it."
*[[Endor]] (10 levels): "The Empire has set up a massive [[Deflector shield generator|shield generator]] on this small forest [[moon]] near the [[Outer Rim Territories|Outer Rim]], but the Rebel Alliance has sent a covert strike team to attack and [[Battle of Endor|destroy]] the Imperial outpost."
*[[Geonosis]] (10 levels): "When it is discovered that massive [[droid]] foundries are creating the [[Separatist Droid Army|Separatist droid army]] led by [[Count]] [[Dooku]], the [[Galactic Republic]] dispatches the [[Jedi]] to the arid desert world to [[First Battle of Geonosis|destroy]] the operation altogether."
*[[Felucia]] (10 levels): "The dense and humid Outer Rim [[planet]] becomes a battleground for control of the galaxy's trade routes as [[Galactic Republic|Republic]] and [[Confederacy of Independent Systems|Separatist]] forces fight to secure the advantage in a never-ending battle."
*[[Kashyyyk]] (10 levels): "The [[wroshyr tree]] covered [[Wookiee]] home planet is a major hub in the [[Mid Rim Territories|Mid Rim]] section of the galaxy. When the Separatists invade, the Republic is threatened with the loss of the crucial system."
*[[Coruscant]] (10 levels): "As the [[capital]] city of the Galactic Republic, Coruscant is residence to many [[senator]]s and the [[Supreme Chancellor]] himself. The Separatist special forces will attempt to disrupt the power of the [[Galactic Senate|Senate]]."

==Continuity==
''Star Wars: Galactic Defense'' contained numerous [[Easter egg (virtual)|Easter eggs]] referencing [[Star Wars Legends|''Star Wars'' Legends]] media. Some vehicles in the game (such as the [[MLC-3 light tank]]) were based on [[Kenner Products|Kenner's]] [[Mini-Rigs]] toy line. Another example is [[Tarfful]] yelling "hnn-rowr yrroonn nng rarr," a quote which first appeared in the Legends comic ''[[Star Wars: Empire's End]]'' and meant "long live the [[New Republic]]" in [[Shyriiwook]]. In the limited-time event "Jedi Hunt," two new playable characters were added to the game—a gray-haired [[Obi-Wan Kenobi|Ben Kenobi]], and [[Maul|Darth Maul]] with [[Cybernetics|cybernetic]] legs—a reference to the ''[[Star Wars: Visionaries]]'' comic ''[[Old Wounds]]''.

Despite the game not having any official content from [[Star Wars: Episode VII The Force Awakens|''Star Wars: The Force Awakens'']], it contains two unintentional nods to [[Ben Solo|Kylo Ren]]. One is found in the Champion description for [[Luke Skywalker]] in his Jedi clothing, which talks of how he plans to "finish what he started" (which is similar to what Ren says in the film's official trailer), referring to early speculation that Luke was actually Ren, which was ultimately disproven. The other one is an in-game glitch that occurs during intense battles involving ranged units firing a huge number of blaster bolts at each other, in which some of the bolts freeze in midair for the rest of the level. This is one of Ren's unique [[The Force|Force]] abilities.

The game also introduces several never-before-seen units, like the [[B1 grapple droid|B1 Grapple Droid]].
